title: Reading a genotype
objective: Decode genotype shorthand: driver, floxed-STOP/LSL, reporter locus, and what cells will be labeled.

steps.title: The shorthand
steps.body:
A genotype is just driver + responder written together, separated by semicolons. Example:

**`Bmpr1b-Cre; Rosa26^LSL-tdTomato`**

- `Bmpr1b-Cre` → the driver ([[Cre]] where Bmpr1b is expressed).
- `Rosa26^LSL-tdTomato` → a tdTomato [[reporter]] at the **Rosa26** locus (a 'safe harbor' that expresses broadly), behind an **LSL**.

steps.title: LSL = Lox-STOP-Lox = floxed STOP
steps.body: **LSL** means a STOP cassette flanked by [[loxP]] sites. It blocks expression of whatever follows until Cre deletes it. 'LSL', 'floxed-STOP', and 'loxP-STOP-loxP' all mean the same thing. So `Rosa26^LSL-tdTomato` is silent everywhere **except** where Cre has acted.

steps.prompt: Match each piece of shorthand to what it means.
pairs: Cre made wherever that gene is expressed
Expression blocked until Cre removes the STOP
Safe-harbor locus used to park reporters/tools
The payload — here, a red fluorophore
steps.explanation: Driver decides WHERE; the floxed STOP decides that the payload is OFF until Cre; the locus is just where the payload lives.

steps.prompt: In `TH-CreER; Rosa26^LSL-GCaMP6f`, what will express the calcium sensor GCaMP6f (after Cre is active)?
options: Only cells given tamoxifen, regardless of TH
steps.explanation: The driver (TH-[[CreER]]) restricts Cre to TH+ cells; the LSL keeps GCaMP6f off until Cre removes the STOP there. (The 'ER' + [[tamoxifen]] part — timing — is the next lesson.)

variants.setup: A TH-CreER; Rosa26-LSL-GCaMP6f mouse is given tamoxifen in adulthood.
variants.prompt: Which cells will express the GCaMP6f sensor?
options: Only cells given tamoxifen, regardless of TH
variants.reveal: CreER needs both the TH promoter and tamoxifen, so GCaMP turns on only in TH cells active when tamoxifen was given.

steps.scenario: A reporter cross labels far MORE cells than the marker gene is expressed in adults.
options: The reporter allele itself is broken and mislabels random cells
Plain Cre also fired in development, when the gene was broader
Too little tamoxifen was given to restrict the labeling
The Rosa26 reporter locus is silent in these neurons
steps.explanation: Plain (constitutive) Cre records any cell that EVER expressed the gene, including transient developmental expression. The fix — restricting Cre to a chosen time window — is exactly what CreER gives you (next lesson).
steps.followUp: This is why 'lineage' labeling (all cells that ever expressed X) differs from 'adult' labeling.

sources.citation: Qi L, et al. A mouse DRG genetic toolkit reveals morphological and physiological diversity of somatosensory neuron subtypes. Cell 187:1508-1526 (2024).
sources.note: Good real-world example of reporter/driver lines across DRG subtypes.
